reviewType: author code-and-evidence review for current material wording

claims.claim: Registered payments reserve a shared root budget and a session budget before exposing a payment signature.
claims.limit: Occupied authorization is not escrowed cash or actual Echo swap spend; unknown commitments remain occupied.

claims.claim: Financial authorization binds exact request, quote, merchant, amount, step, version, session and chain/wallet domain.
claims.limit: Binding hashes does not establish merchant HTTPS origin or usefulness of an arbitrary hidden result.

claims.claim: Deterministic business-step nonces, persisted transactions and reconciliation prevent duplicate payment in the tested retries.
claims.limit: Finite observed scenarios and configured canonical RPC assumptions; not a proof for every token, chain or external merchant.

claims.claim: Settlement rechecks live authority; revocation after facilitator prevalidation can prevent payment.
claims.limit: Revocation does not refund completed transfers; reference facilitator/token compatibility has its own support matrix.

claims.claim: Replacement preserves occupancy/used steps and invalidates old sessions; safe release needs strict expiry and an unused token nonce.
claims.limit: A paid, consumed or uncertain nonce is not automatically a refund; a valid permission can lack cash after an owner withdrawal.

claims.claim: Payment, service delivery and result validation are separate observed states.
claims.limit: A successful HTTP response, token receipt or merchant signature alone does not establish all three.

claims.claim: Selective disclosure preserves disclosed commitments and financial association, while hidden results and HTTPS/history guarantees remain incomplete.
claims.limit: The deployed account does not enforce the entire session root. A signed merchant receipt does not cover every request/result/payment field.

claims.claim: A separately trusted retained latest head detects omission of its known tail; unanchored valid prefixes can hide an unknown tail.
claims.limit: Same-host controller/notary processes do not isolate a malicious administrator or account for all hidden model/network calls.

claims.claim: Owner signing is separate from production Agent/MCP, and actual native MetaMask automation exercised the owner flow.
claims.limit: Local test roles and automated narrow-screen views are not manual usability, physical-mobile acceptance or hostile-host isolation. Hosted-loopback allowance/denial is automated Chromium evidence with Site service access; human login/Owner usability and physical-mobile coverage are not accepted. The current connection-guidance amendment is outside rc6. The final r6 harness uses native Chromium HTTP with per-request CDP headers: same-origin redirects remain, cross-origin redirects are rejected before transmission; a canary destination receives zero requests.

claims.claim: The independent-tool review tracks 113 initial findings and one repaired Echo GCM tag-policy defect, retaining 112 raw signals.
claims.limit: Author triage, static tools and finite tests do not constitute a non-author human audit, zero-findings claim or universal proof. The 113/112 counts describe the original fixed M7 review. A later purchase-feedback scan has 67 TypeScript signals plus 48 contract signals, with three additional HTML-template occurrences reviewed separately. The later TypeScript-only recheck has 67 raw signals with unchanged rule/path multiplicities; unchanged contract fingerprints reuse earlier scans.

claims.claim: Public payments use actual Base native test USDC or the labeled Ethereum TestUSDC fixture; local timings are reported separately.
claims.limit: Controlled loopback merchant/reference facilitator, no third-party merchant purchase or mainnet spending. Two RPCs do not provide independent consensus verification.

claims.claim: Echo reuse, M2 repairs, new Mandate behavior and proposal research questions have distinct implementation/evidence scopes.
claims.limit: Original baseline failures are preserved. Manual formal arguments are not machine proofs; actual registration and reuse authorization require separate evidence.
